study type: Quasi-experimental difference-in-differences evaluation using repeated cross-sectional data
exposure: Removal of user fees for facility-based delivery services
outcome: Proportion of births delivered in facilities
Proportion of births delivered by Caesarean section
cohort: Live births from 10 sub-Saharan African countries between 1997 and 2012, with Kenya, Ghana, and Senegal as intervention countries and seven others as controls.
finding: Removing user fees for facility-based deliveries was associated with an increase of 3.1 facility-based deliveries per 100 live births and an estimated reduction of 2.9 neonatal deaths per 1000 births.
mod_finding: There was no evidence of an increase in Caesarean deliveries following the removal of user fees.
country: 10 sub-Saharan African countries (Kenya, Ghana, Senegal, and seven unspecified control countries)
